narrative:
The model estimates a 37.0% chance that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is a clear warning: roughly one in three students with a similar profile would not pass, so the school is requiring remedial courses to reduce that risk.

The strongest reason for the warning is your history of past class failures. You have three previous failures, while students who passed averaged none, so this factor weighs heavily toward failing. The next two most influential factors actually work in your favor: not having attended nursery school and having low free time both leaned the prediction toward passing rather than failing. Even so, they were not enough to offset the concern created by your failure history.

Other parts of your profile add context. You study less than two hours a week, while most students who passed study two to five hours; you have six absences, above the average of about four; and your weekend alcohol consumption is very high, which is rare among students who passed. You also lack home internet, which may make independent study harder.

Use the remedial courses to address the main risk directly: build a regular study routine, attend every class, reduce weekend drinking, and ask your family and teachers for structured help. Your family support and wish to continue to higher education are strengths you can use.
